input.claim_text: On 9 February 2024 I woke up to find someone had spray-painted graffiti all over our front fence and garage door overnight. It looks like it happened while we were asleep since there was nothing there when we went to bed. I haven't had anyone come out to quote on repainting or replacing the panels yet, so I don't have a cost figure at this stage.

output.cause: spray-paint graffiti on front fence and garage door

input.query: Is vandalism or malicious damage (graffiti) to fences and garage doors covered?

output.answer:
Based on the provided excerpts, I can partially answer this question.

**Malicious damage/vandalism coverage:** Malicious damage is covered as a "deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism and a malicious act)" [NRMA Home KFS, page 1], provided it is not committed by "You, Your Family or anyone who normally lives in Your Home including a tenant" [NRMA Home KFS, page 1; NRMA Home PDS, page 13]. This cover applies to "Your Home if You have 'Building' insurance" and "Your General Contents while in Your Home if You have 'Contents' insurance" [NRMA Home PDS, page 13].

**Specific to fences and garage doors:** The excerpts do not explicitly confirm whether fences or garage doors are included within the definition of "Your Home" for the purposes of this malicious damage cover. One excerpt notes that under a different peril (Flood or Rainwater Run-off), there are exclusions for "retaining walls" and "gates, fences or free-standing walls" in certain circumstances [NRMA Home PDS, page 14], but this exclusion appears tied specifically to flood/rainwater damage, not vandalism.

**Reporting requirement:** If a claim is made, "You must report any deliberate or intentional act to the police and provide Us with the report number and details of when and where the report was made" [NRMA Home PDS, page 13, page 28].

**Conclusion:** The excerpts confirm that vandalism/malicious damage to "Your Home" is generally covered (subject to the exclusions on who caused it), but they do not specifically state whether fences and garage doors fall within the definition of "Home" for this cover, nor do they explicitly address graffiti as a form of damage. I cannot confirm coverage specifically for fences and garage doors based on the excerpts provided — additional policy definitions (e.g., how "Home" is defined, or any specific exclusions for fences/gates under the malicious damage section) would be needed to give a complete answer.
